name: Introduction / Movement & Coordination
who_text: Ages 5-8 (owner Pathway band; PPBF youth entry starts at 5 per Jason, 2026-10-23); band is a guide: placement uses age, experience and athletic ability (placement rule)
develops_text: Fun, movement, coordination, listening; confidence/discipline/respect foundations
competition_text: none. USA Boxing registration starts at age 8, so no sanctioned competition in this band. Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Foundations
who_text: Ages 8-12 (owner Pathway); band is a guide: placement uses age, experience and athletic ability (placement rule)
competition_text: optional, only for prepared athletes (owner policy). If the member competes on the USA Boxing youth route (e.g. Silver Gloves), USA Boxing youth rules are requirements on that route (age classes, bout length, registration); otherwise none apply. Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

competition_text: optional, only for prepared athletes (owner policy). If the member competes on the USA Boxing youth route (e.g. Silver Gloves), USA Boxing youth rules are requirements on that route (age classes, bout length, registration); otherwise none apply. competition_text: optional, only for prepared athletes (owner policy). If the member competes on the USA Boxing youth route (e.g. Silver Gloves), USA Boxing youth rules are requirements on that route (age classes, bout length, registration); otherwise none apply. Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Competition Readiness
who_text: Ages 16-18 (owner Pathway); Curriculum doc also bands 16-18 as 'Competitive preparation'; band is a guide: placement uses age, experience and athletic ability (placement rule)
competition_text: optional/required depending on member goal; USA Boxing Youth division (17-18) rules apply as requirements if member competes on that route (registration, passbook, bout format). Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Foundation
who_text: Adult beginners enter here; also youth graduating Y5; owner decision: adult beginners enter at trunk Novice stage
develops_text: Body tolerance to boxing training, non-liability technical base, aerobic engine, strength foundation, habit system
competition_text: optional; first bout typically months 9-18; USA Boxing rules are requirements only if member competes on that route (Novice class). Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Competitive Amateur
develops_text: Maximal/explosive/reactive strength, high aerobic capacity, buffering capacity, primary style + second gear, systematic preparation (camps, tapers, film study)
competition_text: required in the sense of progression (6-10 bouts/yr, Novice->Open); USA Boxing rules are requirements on that competition route (experience classes: Novice until 10 bouts, Open at 11+, Elite option at 21+). Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: National Amateur
who_text: Years 4-7 from start; Phase 3A High-level amateur
develops_text: National championship competition, tactical flexibility, peaking physical qualities, camp periodization, opponent-specific prep, career infrastructure, tournament readiness (3-5 bouts/week capacity)
competition_text: required for progression; USA Boxing / World Boxing rules are requirements on this route (national championships, international selection); international governance is unstable, verify current structure before multi-year plans. Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: International Amateur
develops_text: Repeatable expression of high ceiling, career longevity, neurological preservation, opponent-specific prep, reliable peaking 2-4 events/yr
competition_text: required; World Boxing / Olympic pathway rules apply on that route (governance in flux; verify before planning). Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Masters (USA Boxing definition)
who_text: USA Boxing Masters: age 41+; boxers 35-40 declare Elite, Masters or both each year
develops_text: Repeatable expression of high ceiling, career longevity, neurological preservation, opponent-specific prep, reliable peaking 2-4 events/yr
competition_text: optional; USA Boxing Masters rules are requirements on the USA Boxing route. Event-specific age rules (for example Junior Olympics or national tournaments) come from each event's Fact Sheet, which USA Boxing treats as an extension of the rule book (Rule 7.4, 2026).

name: Amateur-to-Pro Transition
who_text: Amateur boxer electing to turn pro; readiness ideally meets 5 of 6 criteria (25+ ama bouts or 15+ with dominance, Open/Elite success, Phase 3 physical KPIs, 3 consecutive camps completed, pro-standard team, 18-24mo financial runway)
develops_text: Remove amateur-only habits, build adult pro operating discipline: scoring with position, longer-round composure, defense after offense, exits, aerobic support, controlled contact
typical_duration_text: Months 1-9 of transition program (round extension 1-3, pacing/format 4-6, consolidation 7-9)
competition_text: pro bout; governed by the state athletic commission where the bout happens (to be confirmed per commission)

name: Early Pro / Debut
develops_text: Safe repeatable adult pro identity: jab, rear-hand discipline, defense-to-counter, corner/rope safety, simple fight plan
typical_duration_text: not stated numerically; round distance 4-6 per bout
competition_text: pro bout; state athletic commission where bout occurs governs (to be confirmed)

name: Developmental Pro
develops_text: Stance matchups, inside/control work, body-head layers, opponent-style drills
competition_text: pro bout; state athletic commission where bout occurs governs (to be confirmed)

name: Prospect
who_text: Pro boxer sharpening tactical depth vs better resistance
develops_text: Scouting, opponent-specific constraints, pressure/counterpuncher/tall-jabber/shell responses, harder governed contact only if gates known
competition_text: pro bout; state athletic commission where bout occurs governs (to be confirmed)

name: Contender
who_text: Pro boxer preparing for 8-12 round elite-level demand
develops_text: Plan compression, tactical contingencies, recovery management, commission compliance, elite sparring governance
competition_text: pro bout, 8-12 round distance; state athletic commission where bout occurs governs, plus sanctioning body rules (to be confirmed)

name: Recreational Boxing (Lifelong)
who_text: Any member, any age, training boxing with contact but not seeking competition; includes members who do both fitness and contact training
develops_text: Fitness, skill mastery, confidence, discipline, lifelong engagement; life-skill transfer
competition_text: No competition required. PPBF runs USA Boxing and other programs: a recreational member in the USA Boxing program follows USA Boxing club rules and spars only USA Boxing members; in other programs PPBF defaults apply.

name: Fitness (Lifelong, non-contact)
who_text: Any member, any age, using boxing for fitness and technique without contact
develops_text: Boxing-based conditioning, technique on bags, pads and shadow work, coordination and general fitness
competition_text: none; no governing body applies to in-gym fitness training (to be confirmed in the evidence pass)

name: Exit: Retirement & Transition
who_text: Any athlete at any stage choosing or needing to stop competitive/contact training
develops_text: Transition into coaching, officiating, or continued non-competitive gym membership; identity/financial/education planning parallel throughout career, not deferred
